transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says the Trump administration has warned it could cut off intelligent sharing
unless the country stops drone strikes on Russian oil refineries.
NPR's Joanna Kakissa spoke to Volodymyr Zelensky.
Zelensky told NPR that the Trump administration's decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel
will not bring down fuel prices.
He says the Iran war has blocked fuel transport through the Strait of Hormuz.
Mostly people in the world know why their prices on any kind of energy, including diesel, raised up.
Why they increased.
Because of blocking the Strait of Hormuz.
Everybody understands that.
President Trump blames Ukraine for rising diesel prices.
He has demanded Ukraine stop its deep strikes on Russian energy sites.
Zelensky says Ukraine wants to weaken the Kremlin's ability to wage war.
He says Ukraine will not stop these strikes unless Russia also stops attacking Ukraine's energy grid.
Joanna Kakissa, NPR News, Kyiv.
Earlier today, President Zelensky said Ukraine received no advance warning from Western allies about Russian missiles headed to Kyiv.
On Telegram, Zelensky said the main target was energy infrastructure.
President Trump says the U.S. has not stopped sharing intelligence.
Cornell University has suspended parties at fraternity houses for the rest of the academic year,
among other changes in response to a student's allegations of gang rape in October 2024.
Then here's Alyssa Nadmorny reports.
The university announced a number of changes to strengthen campus safety and better support sexual assault survivors.
In addition to banning all parties and social events at fraternity houses,
the Ivy League school will also hire staff to help students navigate reporting sexual misconduct
and will hire criminal investigators independent of Cornell to investigate allegations of sexual assault on campus.
In a letter to the campus, the school's president, Michael Kotlikoff, writes,
"Cornell must be a place where safety is not an open question."
The changes come amid continued frustration and protests from students and faculty on the handling of Jane Doe's 2024 case.
Alyssa Nadmorny, NPR News, Ithaca, New York.
Pope Leo has been diagnosed with lung cancer, NPR's Lee Hale reports on the news after Leo underwent surgery in Rome earlier today.
The surgery wasn't a surprise.
Pope Leo announced over the weekend that a nodule would be removed from his lung.
But after the 90-minute operation, the Vatican provided an update and a diagnosis.
Adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer.
The medical team says part of the right lung was removed.
At 71, Leo is young for a pope and exercises regularly.
The Vatican is yet to announce any further treatments.
Leo will spend the rest of the week resting at the hospital.
His schedule has been cleared up of any public events until at least October 20th.
Lee Hale, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News.
President Trump is to spend the night in Las Vegas after speaking at a campaign rally in Alaska
where he was stumping for Republican Senator Dan Sullivan.
Speaking in Wasilla, Trump's remarks lasted nearly 90 minutes.
During his speech, a president announced that Taiwan has agreed to buy 30% of the gas from a pipeline project in Alaska.
The terms of the deal are not clear.
The man convicted of orchestrating the murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur has been sentenced to 40 years to life in prison.
A jury in Las Vegas handed the sentence to Dwayne Davis today. Davis was convicted of first degree murder with a deadly weapon in late August.
NASA's Mars Rover Perseverance just logged a major milestone, the longest total drive distance by a vehicle on another world.
Here's NPR's Ari Daniel reporting.
That distance is 28 miles, which may not seem like much by earthly standards.
But project scientist Katie Stack Morgan says it's a big deal for an off-world rover.
This is the culmination of how we explore the solar system and the capabilities that we bring to other planets.
Over the last half decade, Perseverance has collected possible evidence of life in Jezero Crater
and sampled rocks that might represent the first half billion years of solar system history.
It collected material from the Martian surface so that one day another mission might return those samples to Earth.
But this part of the program has an uncertain future,
given its hefty price tag put it in the crosshairs of the federal government earlier this year.
Ari Daniel, NPR News.
And I'm Giles Snyder. This is NPR News.

topics.text: Zelensky says Trump administration warned it could cut intelligence sharing over Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries
Zelensky tells NPR lifting Russian diesel sanctions won't lower fuel prices due to Strait of Hormuz blockage
Trump blames Ukraine for rising diesel prices and demands it stop deep strikes on Russian energy sites
Zelensky says Ukraine received no Western warning about Russian missiles aimed at Kyiv energy infrastructure
Cornell suspends fraternity house parties for rest of year, adds sexual assault support and independent investigators
Pope Leo undergoes lung surgery in Rome, diagnosed with adenocarcinoma, part of right lung removed
Trump campaigns in Wasilla, Alaska for Senator Dan Sullivan, announces Taiwan will buy Alaska pipeline gas
Dwayne Davis sentenced to 40 years to life for orchestrating Tupac Shakur's murder
Mars rover Perseverance sets record for longest total driving distance by a vehicle on another world
